#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Daily release-draft sweeper (issue #282), rides daily-publish.yml:
#
#   - lists DRAFT releases older than $SWEEP_MAX_AGE_SECONDS (default 24h);
#   - deletes stale drafts created by the pipeline (author.type == Bot, a
#     *[bot] login, OR the body carries a well-formed
#     `release-draft-owner: run/<id>/job/<job>` marker — the exact shape
#     release_lazy_draft.sh / release_attach_or_create.sh stamp and
#     release_draft_guard.sh parses; since the drafts are created with
#     GH_TOKEN=RELEASE_PAT the API author is the PAT's human owner, so
#     the marker is the only ownership proof, gh-2008. Prose that merely
#     MENTIONS the substring or a malformed marker is NOT ownership —
#     those drafts stay human/kept, E1) — draft assets are unpublished by
#     definition and published releases are the artifact store, so
#     deletion is safe (issue #282 E2). The git tag is never touched;
#   - stale HUMAN drafts are listed in the summary, never deleted (E1);
#   - fresh drafts (<24h) are counted, never touched — an in-flight run
#     may legitimately own them;
#   - files ONE deduplicated, self-closing issue (label release-hygiene)
#     whenever anything stale was found — a comment on the open issue
#     instead of a duplicate, auto-closed again once a sweep comes up
#     clean (same convention as nightly.yml / daily_publish_report.sh).
#
# Drafts are deleted by release id via the API: a draft may carry an empty
# tag_name, which makes every tag-based `gh release delete` ambiguous.
#
# Env: GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GH_TOKEN, SWEEP_MAX_AGE_SECONDS (default 86400),
#      SWEEP_LABEL (default release-hygiene).
set -euo pipefail

repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
max_age="${SWEEP_MAX_AGE_SECONDS:-86400}"
label="${SWEEP_LABEL:-release-hygiene}"
title="[daily-publish] stale release drafts swept"
daily_url="${GITHUB_SERVER_URL:-https://github.com}/$repo/actions/runs/${GITHUB_RUN_ID:-manual}"

gh label create "$label" --repo "$repo" --color B60205 \
  --description "Auto-filed by the release-draft sweeper" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

# ── inventory ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# gh api --paginate emits one JSON array per page; the jq stream filter
# flattens them all. Bucketing happens in jq so the whole rule is
# reviewable in one place:
#   stale + pipeline (bot author or well-formed
#                    release-draft-owner: run/<id>/job/<job>
#                    marker in the body) -> delete, name the marker run
#   stale + human (no marker)          -> keep, list
#   fresh                              -> untouched
drafts=$(gh api --paginate "repos/$repo/releases" | jq -r --argjson maxage "$max_age" '
  [ .[] | select(.draft == true)
    | { bucket: (
          if ((now - (.created_at | fromdateiso8601)) > $maxage)
          then (if ((.author.type // "User") == "Bot"
                    or ((.author.login // "") | test("\\[bot\\]$"))
                    or ((.body // "") | test("release-draft-owner: run/[0-9]+/job/")))
               then "bot" else "human" end)
          else "fresh" end),
        tag: (.tag_name // "(untagged)"),
        id: (.id | tostring),
        created: (.created_at // "?"),
        author: (.author.login // "unknown"),
        # Exact creating run parsed from the ownership marker ("" for
        # non-marker drafts) — the creating run executed on main, so a
        # tag-ref run lookup cannot find it (gh-2008). The array wrapper
        # keeps exactly one value: a bare capture(...)? on a non-matching
        # body yields an EMPTY stream, and an empty field would drop the
        # whole draft row from the object stream.
        run: ([ (.body // "")
                | capture("release-draft-owner: run/(?<run>[0-9]+)/")?
                | .run ]
              | .[0] // "") } ]
  | sort_by(.created)[]
  | [ .bucket, .tag, .id, .created, .author, .run ] | @tsv')

deleted=""
deleted_tags=""
deleted_count=0
failed_trains=0
humans=""
human_tags=""
fresh_count=0

while IFS=$'\t' read -r bucket tag id created author marker_run; do
  [ -n "$bucket" ] || continue
  case "$bucket" in
    fresh)
      fresh_count=$((fresh_count + 1))
      ;;
    human)
      humans="$humans- \`$tag\` — created $created by @$author (human draft: listed, kept)\n"
      human_tags="$human_tags $tag"
      ;;
    bot)
      gh api -X DELETE "repos/$repo/releases/$id" >/dev/null
      deleted_count=$((deleted_count + 1))
      # Name the creating run so a RECURRING stuck draft points at its
      # broken step instead of rotting silently (AC2). Marker drafts name
      # it exactly (the stamping scripts write run/<id>); untagged
      # author-bot drafts fall back to the newest run on the tag ref;
      # dispatch-time drafts have no run on their ref — then say so.
      run_url=""
      if [ -n "$marker_run" ]; then
        run_url="${GITHUB_SERVER_URL:-https://github.com}/$repo/actions/runs/$marker_run"
      elif [ "$tag" != "(untagged)" ]; then
        run_url=$(gh run list --repo "$repo" --branch "$tag" --limit 1 \
          --json url --jq '.[0].url // empty' 2>/dev/null || true)
      fi
      [ -n "$run_url" ] || run_url="no run on ref \`$tag\` (dispatch-time draft — the creating step died mid-run)"
      # gh-2105: the staging draft's publish owner is the TAG TRAIN
      # (ci.yml's push run on the tag ref — release-provenance is the
      # sole publish point, gh-1801). When that train failed, the
      # creating run named above is NOT the broken step — the train is,
      # and a superseded failed train is never rerun
      # (verify_pubdev_release.sh heals the LATEST tag only). Name it
      # (URL + conclusion + failed jobs) so the sweep issue points at
      # the true blocker. Any lookup failure degrades to the static
      # prose below — the delete + issue filing must never depend on
      # the diagnosis.
      train_line=""
      if [ "$tag" != "(untagged)" ]; then
        train_json=$(gh run list --repo "$repo" --workflow ci.yml \
          --branch "$tag" --event push --limit 5 \
          --json databaseId,conclusion,url 2>/dev/null || echo "[]")
        failed_train=$(printf '%s' "$train_json" | jq -cr '
          ([.[] | select(.conclusion != "success" and .conclusion != null)][0]
            | if . == null then empty else
                {c: .conclusion, u: (.url // ""), i: .databaseId}
              end)' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
        if [ -n "$failed_train" ]; then
          train_conclusion=$(printf '%s' "$failed_train" | jq -r '.c // "unknown"' 2>/dev/null || echo "unknown")
          train_url_found=$(printf '%s' "$failed_train" | jq -r '.u // ""' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
          train_id=$(printf '%s' "$failed_train" | jq -r '.i // ""' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
          failed_jobs=$(gh run view "$train_id" --repo "$repo" --json jobs 2>/dev/null \
            | jq -r '[.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "failure") | .name] | join(", ")' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
          failed_trains=$((failed_trains + 1))
          train_line="  - tag train: ${train_url_found:-<url unavailable>} concluded ${train_conclusion:-unknown} — the staged draft was never published (release-provenance, the sole publish point, is gated behind the tag train; a superseded failed train is never rerun — verify_pubdev_release.sh heals the LATEST tag only)"
          [ -n "$failed_jobs" ] && train_line="$train_line; failed jobs: $failed_jobs"
          train_line="$train_line\n"
        fi
      fi
      deleted="$deleted- \`$tag\` — created $created by @$author; creating run: $run_url\n$train_line"
      deleted_tags="$deleted_tags $tag"
      ;;
  esac
done <<< "$drafts"

# ── issue lifecycle (dedup + self-closing) ─────────────────────────────────
find_open_issue() { # echoes the issue number of the open sweep issue, or nothing
  gh issue list --repo "$repo" --state open --label "$label" \
    --limit 100 --json number,title --jq '.[] | [.number, .title] | @tsv' 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS=$'\t' read -r n t; do
        if [ "$t" = "$title" ]; then echo "$n"; fi
      done | head -1
}

stale_count=$((deleted_count + $(printf '%s' "$humans" | grep -c . || true) ))

if [ "$stale_count" -gt 0 ]; then
  body=$(mktemp)
  {
    echo "**Sweep run:** $daily_url"
    echo "**Swept:** $deleted_count stale pipeline-created draft(s) older than $((max_age / 3600))h"
    printf '%b' "$deleted"
    [ -n "$humans" ] && { echo; echo "**Kept (human drafts, listed not deleted — E1):**"; printf '%b' "$humans"; }
    echo
    echo "**Fresh drafts (<$((max_age / 3600))h):** $fresh_count — untouched (an in-flight run may own them)"
    echo
    if [ "$failed_trains" -gt 0 ]; then
      echo "**Failed tag trains named above:** $failed_trains"
      echo
      echo "A stale draft whose tag train failed means the publish owner never ran — the draft was the gh-1801 staging draft and release-provenance (its sole publish point) is gated behind the failed train. Rerun the train if the tag should still ship; recurrence means a lifecycle guard is missing (issue #282)."
    else
      echo "A stale draft means a \`gh release create\` step died between asset upload and publish — check the creating run's failed step. Recurrence means a lifecycle guard is missing (issue #282)."
    fi
    echo
    echo "---"
    echo "Auto-filed by the daily draft sweeper; auto-closes when a sweep finds nothing stale."
  } > "$body"
  existing=$(find_open_issue)
  if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
    gh issue comment "$existing" --repo "$repo" --body-file "$body" >/dev/null
    issue_action="commented on #$existing (still finding stale drafts)"
  else
    created_issue=$(gh issue create --repo "$repo" --title "$title" \
      --body-file "$body" --label bug --label "$label" --assignee ai-teammate 2>/dev/null || true)
    issue_action="filed ${created_issue:-<issue creation failed>}"
  fi
  rm -f "$body"
else
  existing=$(find_open_issue)
  issue_action="none needed"
  if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
    gh issue close "$existing" --repo "$repo" \
      --comment "✅ sweep found nothing stale — auto-closing." >/dev/null
    issue_action="auto-closed #$existing (clean sweep)"
  fi
fi

# ── job summary ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
{
  echo "### Release-draft sweeper"
  echo
  echo "Deleted **$deleted_count** stale pipeline-created draft(s) • failed tag trains named: **$failed_trains** • kept human drafts: **$(printf '%s' "$humans" | grep -c . || true)** • fresh (<$((max_age / 3600))h): **$fresh_count** • issue lifecycle: $issue_action"
} >> "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY:-/dev/stdout}"

echo "sweeper: deleted=${deleted_tags# } human-kept=${human_tags# } fresh=$fresh_count issue=$issue_action"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Release draft lifecycle guard (issue #282): a run that creates a release
# draft must end with it published or deleted — never orphan it. `gh
# release create <tag> <assets...>` uploads the assets through a DRAFT
# first and publishes only after every upload succeeds; a step dying
# mid-upload (the v0.1.190 rot) leaves that draft behind forever.
#
# Usage: release_draft_guard.sh <tag>
#
# OWNERSHIP-SCOPED DELETE (review of #294): the guard deletes ONLY the
# draft this very run+job created. daily-publish runs the macOS and
# mobile legs concurrently against the same derived tag; a failed leg's
# guard firing on the SIBLING leg's mid-upload draft would destroy a
# healthy concurrent release. Draft-capable creates
# (scripts/release_attach_or_create.sh, scripts/release_lazy_draft.sh)
# stamp the draft body with
#   <!-- release-draft-owner: run/<run_id>/job/<job_id> -->
# and the guard deletes only on an exact match against GITHUB_RUN_ID /
# GITHUB_JOB (both GitHub Actions default env). Matrix jobs share
# GITHUB_JOB across legs (ci.yml binaries, build-macos.yml
# build-macos-cli) — those steps stamp a LEG-SUFFIXED identity via
# RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY (e.g. run/123/job/binaries-linux-x64) and the
# guard step must export the same value, so a failed leg can never match
# a sibling's in-flight draft. A foreign or unmarked draft is NEVER
# deleted here — the daily sweeper
# (scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh) reclaims genuinely orphaned drafts
# after 24h.
#
# Called from workflow steps with `if: always() && job.status != 'success'`
# so it runs on failure AND cancellation. A published release or a missing
# release is a no-op; a draft for <tag> is deleted (its assets are
# unpublished by definition — published releases are the artifact store,
# issue #282 E2). The tag itself is never touched.
set -euo pipefail

tag="${1:?usage: release_draft_guard.sh <tag>}"
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
: "${GITHUB_RUN_ID:?GITHUB_RUN_ID must be set (GitHub Actions default env)}"
: "${GITHUB_JOB:?GITHUB_JOB must be set (GitHub Actions default env)}"
identity="${RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY:-run/$GITHUB_RUN_ID/job/$GITHUB_JOB}"
# Validate (mirror of release_lazy_draft.sh): an unmatchable identity
# would silently orphan the draft forever.
printf '%s' "$identity" | grep -Eq '^run/[0-9]+/job/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$' || {
  echo "::error::RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY '$identity' does not match 'run/<id>/job/<name>' — the marker could never be stamped or matched" >&2
  exit 1
}

state=$(gh release view "$tag" --repo "$repo" --json isDraft --jq .isDraft 2>/dev/null || echo missing)
if [ "$state" != "true" ]; then
  echo "release lifecycle guard: $tag is ${state} (published or absent) — nothing to clean"
  exit 0
fi

notes=$(gh release view "$tag" --repo "$repo" --json body --jq '.body // ""' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
owner=$(printf '%s' "$notes" \
  | grep -oE 'release-draft-owner: run/[0-9]+/job/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+' \
  | head -1 | sed 's/^release-draft-owner: //' || true)

if [ "$owner" != "$identity" ]; then
  echo "::warning::release lifecycle guard: draft $tag is owned by '${owner:-<unmarked>}' (we are $identity) — refusing to delete a draft this run+job did not create; a sibling leg may be mid-upload. The daily sweeper reclaims orphaned drafts after 24h (issue #282)."
  exit 0
fi

gh release delete "$tag" --repo "$repo" --yes
echo "::warning::release lifecycle guard: deleted own draft $tag — the run failed after creating it; a draft must be published or deleted, never orphaned (issue #282)"

(not just legs) files its own
`[daily-publish] plan leg failed` issue — nothing escapes the loop.

## Self-healing issues

On a failing (or timed-out) leg the `report` job files an issue:

- title `[daily-publish] <leg> leg failed`, label `bug` + `daily-publish`,
  assigned to `vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit`;
- body: daily run link, leg run link, failing job/step names, the last ~50
  lines of the failed step's log;
- **dedup**: an open issue with the same signature gets a comment instead
  of a duplicate;
- **auto-close**: when the leg goes green in a later daily run, the open
  issue is closed with a comment.

Each run also writes a single job-summary table (leg → version → status →
links) and exits red itself when any leg failed.

## Release hygiene (issue #282)

No orphan drafts, one naming scheme, a truthful `Latest`, useful notes:

- **Draft lifecycle invariant** — every workflow step that creates a
  release draft (`gh release create <tag> <assets…>` uploads assets
  through a *draft* first and only publishes afterwards) is paired with a
  `Draft lifecycle guard` step in the same job:
  `if: always() && job.status != 'success'` + `scripts/release_draft_guard.sh`
  — a failed **or cancelled** run deletes its orphaned draft instead of
  leaving it to rot. The delete is **ownership-scoped** (review of #294):
  the guard only deletes a draft whose body carries this very run+job's
  `<!-- release-draft-owner: run/<id>/job/<job> -->` marker — daily-publish
  runs the mobile and macOS legs concurrently on the same derived tag, and
  a failed leg's guard must never destroy the sibling leg's mid-upload
  draft (foreign or unmarked drafts are left to the sweeper). Pinned by
  `test/release_hygiene_test.dart` (a job with an asset-carrying create
  and no guard fails CI).
- **Attach-or-create** — the draft-capable creates of build-macos.yml /
  build-mobile.yml live in `scripts/release_attach_or_create.sh`, which is
  idempotent under the view→create race (#282 E3): a create that loses to
  a concurrent winner uploads into the winner's release instead of
  failing (a failing create would fire the guard against the winner's
  in-flight draft), and the create stamps the ownership marker the guard
  verifies.
- **Daily sweeper** — the `sweep-drafts` job in `daily-publish.yml` runs
  `scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh` on **every** daily invocation (leg
  results and change-gating never gate hygiene): drafts older than 24h
  are deleted when the PIPELINE created them — a Bot author / `*[bot]`
  login, or the body carries a well-formed
  `release-draft-owner: run/<id>/job/<job>` marker (the drafts
  are created with the owner's RELEASE_PAT, so the API author is a human
  and the marker is the only ownership proof — gh-2008; the bucket rule
  keys on the exact stamped shape, so prose merely mentioning the
  substring or a malformed marker stays human — review thread
  PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6yOzIh; id-based API
  delete, tag and git history untouched — draft assets are unpublished by
  definition, E2), human drafts (no marker) are listed but kept (E1),
  fresh (<24h) drafts are left for their in-flight run. The job grants
  `actions: read` — unmarked swept drafts name their creating run via
  `gh run list`, which 403s without it; marker drafts name the marker's
  run id directly. Anything
  stale files **one** deduplicated `release-hygiene` issue (comment on the
  open one, auto-close on a clean sweep — same convention as the leg
  issues) naming each swept draft and its creating run, so a recurring
  stuck draft points at its broken step. The test stub enforces the
  workflow-declared token permissions, so a dropped grant fails CI instead
  of silently degrading the issue to "no run on ref".
- **Naming** — titles are the bare `vX.Y.Z` tag everywhere (matches the
  tag, matches pub.dev). No `Fa ` prefixes, no untitled creates; both are
  lint-failed by `test/release_hygiene_test.dart`. Pre-existing published
  titles (e.g. `Fa v0.1.362`) are deliberately not rewritten — backfill
  is opt-in per release.
- **Latest** — every publish path passes `--latest` explicitly (and
  re-asserts it via `gh release edit --latest` when attaching to a
  release another path created first). Guards and the sweeper only ever
  delete — a failed run can never capture the badge.
- **Notes** — `scripts/release_notes.sh` renders the curated CHANGELOG.md
  `## <version>` section when one exists, else the curated `## Unreleased`
  body (gh-1522: the release folds Unreleased into the tag's section at
  stage time, never in-repo), else conventional commits since the
  previous tag grouped Features/Fixes/Maintenance (capped at 50 +

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Lazy DRAFT create for the release train's asset-upload steps (gh-1801).
#
# The train workflows (ci.yml binaries/web-spa, build-macos.yml
# build-macos-cli/build-extension) need a release object to attach assets
# to, but the release must never go live from an upload step: `fa update`
# resolves the `latest` release and hard-fails without the SIGNED
# SHA256SUMS(.sig) (bin/self_manage.dart provenance gate), which only the
# tag-run release-provenance job can upload. This script creates the
# release as a DRAFT — nothing else:
#
#   - body = scripts/release_notes.sh output (curated `## <version>`
#     CHANGELOG section → curated `## Unreleased` → conventional commits;
#     the gh-1172 curated-notes contract), with a minimal fallback —
#     never `--generate-notes` (review threads 3/7);
#   - body carries `<!-- release-draft-owner: run/<run_id>/job/<job> -->`
#     so scripts/release_draft_guard.sh can reclaim the draft on failure
#     (review threads 4/8) — matrix legs override the identity via
#     RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY (e.g. binaries-linux-x64) so a failed leg's
#     guard can never match a sibling's in-flight draft;
#   - the view→create race is tolerated (`|| true`): a sibling leg or the
#     attach path may create the release between our view and create —
#     the loser just uploads into the winner's release;
#   - it NEVER publishes and NEVER flags latest: the single publish point
#     of a tag train is release-provenance's "Upload provenance assets"
#     step (`gh release edit --draft=false --latest` after SHA256SUMS.sig
#     lands). A red provenance leaves the previous release as latest —
#     safe degradation, never a provenance-less latest (v1.0.630 window).
#
# Usage: release_lazy_draft.sh <tag>
# Env: GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GITHUB_RUN_ID, GITHUB_JOB (Actions defaults),
#      RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY (optional leg-suffixed override),
#      GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN.
set -euo pipefail

tag="${1:?usage: release_lazy_draft.sh <tag>}"
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"
identity="${RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY:-run/${GITHUB_RUN_ID:?GITHUB_RUN_ID must be set (GitHub Actions default env)}/job/${GITHUB_JOB:?GITHUB_JOB must be set (GitHub Actions default env)}}"

# The guard greps exactly this class — validate here so a malformed
# override fails loud instead of stamping a marker the guard could never
# match (a forever-orphaned draft).
printf '%s' "$identity" | grep -Eq '^run/[0-9]+/job/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$' || {
  echo "::error::RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY '$identity' does not match 'run/<id>/job/<name>' — the draft lifecycle guard could never reclaim such a draft" >&2
  exit 1
}

# Already created (by a sibling leg, the attach path, or a previous run)?
# Drafts and published releases both resolve here — upload-only is safe.
if gh release view "$tag" --repo "$repo" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "release $tag already exists — lazy draft create skipped"
  exit 0
fi

# Body: curated notes (CHANGELOG section / Unreleased / conventional
# commits) plus the ownership marker the guard verifies before deleting.
# stderr is NOT swallowed: release_notes.sh's ::error gates (e.g. the
# duplicate-'## Unreleased' curation guard) must stay visible even when
# the minimal fallback below keeps the train moving.
notes_file="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/release-lazy-notes.XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -f "$notes_file"' EXIT
if ! bash "$(dirname "$0")/release_notes.sh" "$tag" >"$notes_file" ||
  [ ! -s "$notes_file" ]; then
  printf 'Release %s — see the CHANGELOG.\n' "$tag" >"$notes_file"
fi
marker="<!-- release-draft-owner: $identity -->"
grep -qF "$marker" "$notes_file" || printf '\n%s\n' "$marker" >>"$notes_file"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Auto-release (gh-1522): cut the annotated TAG + GitHub Release directly —
# the git tag is the single source of truth for versions and ZERO files are
# mutated in-repo. The retired flow (this script used to patch-bump
# pubspec.yaml / CHANGELOG.md / flutter_app/pubspec.{yaml,lock} and push a
# 'chore(release):' commit straight to protected main) landed a 4-file bot
# commit on main per release: noisy history, a direct-to-main bot push
# path, CHANGELOG growth toward the pub.dev 256 KiB cap (gh-1452), and
# pubspec.lock churn that invalidated flutter_app's --enforce-lockfile
# (gh-1265). Now:
#
#   latest tag + 1  →  `git tag -a v$next origin/main`  →  push the tag
#
# NO GitHub Release is created here (gh-1801): this script has an EMPTY
# resolved asset list, and creating the release would publish an empty
# `latest` that breaks `fa update` until the binaries backfill. The
# tag-run binaries job owns release creation — draft-first, published
# only after an asset upload lands.
#
# Runs in CI on every push to main / the 2h catch-up cron / manual dispatch
# (the `release` job in .github/workflows/ci.yml). The job authenticates via
# actions/create-github-app-token (RELEASE_APP_ID + RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY);
# the App token pushes the tag because GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never trigger the
# tag-scoped publish/binaries jobs (gh-1172). The App remains the ONLY
# bypass actor on the main ruleset but no longer needs to push to main at
# all — releases never touch the branch.
#

# publish tree from the SAME tag (scripts/stage_publish_package.sh <dir>
# <version>) — the tag↔staged-version invariant is guarded there.
#
# Dry-run: RELEASE_DRY_RUN=1 (or "true") computes the tag that WOULD be
# cut, logs it, and stops before any push.
#
# Release notes: scripts/release_notes.sh is NOT invoked here anymore —
# with no release create there is no body to prepare. The release body is
# owned by the tag-run binaries job's lazy draft create
# (scripts/release_lazy_draft.sh), which folds the curated CHANGELOG
# section via release_notes.sh into the DRAFT it creates; the signed
# provenance job publishes it (gh-1801).
set -euo pipefail

# Tag authorship names the App so releases are attributable in history
# (auditability contract, gh-1172).
git config user.name "fa-release-bot[bot]"
git config user.email "fa-release-bot[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"

dry_run=0
case "${RELEASE_DRY_RUN:-0}" in 1|true|yes) dry_run=1 ;; esac

# Coalescing guards: pub.dev rate-limits publishes (~12/day), so releases are
# capped at one per 2h; runs with nothing new since the last tag are skipped.
git fetch origin main --tags --quiet
last_tag=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || true)
if [ -n "$last_tag" ]; then
  pending=$(git rev-list --count "$last_tag..origin/main")
  if [ "$pending" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "Auto-release: nothing new since $last_tag, skipping."
    exit 0
  fi
  # The 2h window runs from the RELEASE, not from the commit the tag points
  # at: commits can sit pending on main for hours before the cron/dispatch
  # cuts the tag (the common catch-up path), and reading the commit date
  # would let extra releases through exactly when this guard (and the
  # pub.dev ~12/day rate limit) exists to stop them (PR #1526 thread 5).
  # Annotated tags carry a tagger date; a lightweight tag (never cut by
  # this script, but defensive) falls back to the commit date.
  tag_ts=$(git for-each-ref --format='%(taggerdate:unix)' "refs/tags/$last_tag")
  [ -n "$tag_ts" ] || tag_ts=$(git log -1 --format=%ct "$last_tag")
  tag_age=$(( $(date +%s) - tag_ts ))
  if [ "$tag_age" -lt 7200 ]; then
    echo "Auto-release: coalesced — $last_tag is ${tag_age}s old (<2h); $pending commit(s) pending. Next eligible push or the 2h cron will release them."
    exit 0
  fi
fi

# the push rejects it (already exists) and the retry loop re-derives from

release-provenance:
    name: Sign release checksums
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [binaries, web-spa, build-extension]
    timeout-minutes: 10
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.binaries.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release')
    permissions:
      contents: write # upload SHA256SUMS(.sig) to the GitHub Release
    steps:
      # gh-814 r2: the trust-anchor drift gate below diffs the secret's public
      # key against the PEM embedded in site/install.sh — that file must be
      # present, so the signing job checks out the site/ tree.
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Collect release assets
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          mkdir -p provenance
          gh release download "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" \
            --dir provenance --pattern 'fa-*'
          ls -l provenance

      # gh-1832: PUBLISH-BLOCKING required-assets gate. The single source of
      # truth is scripts/release_required_assets.txt, consumed by
      # scripts/assert_release_assets.sh. v1.0.635 published without
      # fa-extension.zip because the extension's only producer (the daily
      # build-macos.yml build-extension leg) attached it to a "latest+1"
      # draft while this train published the tagged release — every leg
      # green, nothing asserted the published set. A missing asset here
      # fails the release run loudly and leaves the release a DRAFT (the
      # previous release stays latest) instead of publishing a partial one.
      - name: Assert required release assets (gh-1832 gate)
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: bash scripts/assert_release_assets.sh "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"

      - name: Build and sign SHA256SUMS
        env:
          FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY }}
        run: |
          cd provenance
          sha256sum fa-* > SHA256SUMS
          if [ -z "$FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY" ]; then
            echo "::error::FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY is not set — refusing to publish a release without signed checksums (SEC-07 #795, fail-closed). Set the repo secret with the release-signing private key."
            exit 1
          fi
          printf '%s' "$FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"
          chmod 600 "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"
          # The key never outlives the step — trap covers mid-step failure.
          trap 'rm -f "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"' EXIT
          openssl dgst -sha256 -sign "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key" -out SHA256SUMS.sig SHA256SUMS
          # Self-check: the signature must verify against OUR OWN public key
          # before anything is uploaded.
          openssl rsa -in "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key" -pubout -out pub.pem 2>/dev/null
          openssl dgst -sha256 -verify pub.pem -signature SHA256SUMS.sig SHA256SUMS
          rm -f "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"
          # gh-814 r2 trust-anchor drift gate (fail-closed): the public key
          # derived from the secret must equal the PEM embedded in
          # site/install.sh — otherwise every pinned installer would ship an
          # anchor that rejects this release's signed checksums.
          sed -n '/BEGIN PUBLIC KEY/,/END PUBLIC KEY/p' "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/site/install.sh" |
            sed "1s/^.*BEGIN/-----BEGIN/; \$s/END.*\$/END PUBLIC KEY-----/" > embedded-anchor.pem
          openssl pkey -pubin -in embedded-anchor.pem -noout ||
            { echo "::error::site/install.sh trust anchor does not parse as a public key — regenerate installers (dart run scripts/gen_installers.dart)"; exit 1; }
          cmp embedded-anchor.pem pub.pem ||
            { echo "::error::FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY drifted from the trust anchor embedded in site/install.sh — rotate the keypair: update install.signing_public_key in site/install-config.yaml, regenerate installers, and update the repo secret TOGETHER. Refusing to sign (fail-closed)."; exit 1; }
          rm -f pub.pem embedded-anchor.pem

      - name: Upload provenance assets
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          gh release upload "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" \
            provenance/SHA256SUMS provenance/SHA256SUMS.sig \
            --clobber --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
          # gh-1801 (rework): THE publish point of the train. The release
          # now carries every fa-* asset AND the signed SHA256SUMS(.sig) —
          # the first moment `fa update` can actually serve it (it
          # hard-fails without the signed checksums, bin/self_manage.dart).
          # Flip draft=false + latest here and ONLY here: a red provenance
          # leaves the previous release as latest (safe degradation)
          # instead of stranding a provenance-less one (the v1.0.630
          # empty/partial-latest window class).
          #
          # gh-2042 (BLOCKING review thread): the flip must never drag the
          # `latest` badge backwards. The drift remediation
          # (scripts/release_drift_remediate.sh) re-requests THIS job for
          # an old drifted tag; a job rerun re-executes this step with the
          # original run's ref, and an unconditional --latest would
          # re-flag that older release as Latest — pointing every
          # `fa update` client DOWN at it (the re-signed manifest would
          # make the downgrade pass provenance). Carry --latest ONLY when
          # the release is still a draft (the normal publish point,
          # gh-1801) or already the current latest; otherwise publish the
          # re-signed state without touching the badge.
          is_draft=$(gh release view "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --json isDraft --jq .isDraft)
          current_latest=$(gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/releases/latest" --jq .tag_name 2>/dev/null || true)
          if [ "$is_draft" = "true" ] || [ "$current_latest" = "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" ]; then
            gh release edit "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --draft=false --latest --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
          else
            # Re-sign remediation of a non-latest tag: publish state is
            # already correct — never drag the latest badge backwards
            # (gh-2042).
            gh release edit "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --draft=false --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"
          fi

      # gh-1899: the flip above publishes exactly ONE release object, but
      # GitHub does not atomically enforce one release per tag — two train
      # legs racing the lazy draft create can BOTH succeed (v1.0.641, run
      # 40163369302: twin drafts 87 ms apart), and the unpicked twin then
      # rots until the 24h sweeper deletes it and files a recurring sweep
      # issue. The tag is published and servable now: reclaim this run's
      # twin drafts. Success-path only — a red provenance keeps the draft
      # as the rerun --failed recovery vessel.
      # Best-effort by design (gh-1899 review): the flip above already
      # published the release — a cleanup-only API blip here must NOT fail
      # the provenance job (release-asset-smoke gates on its result and
      # would silently skip for a release that is actually fine). Warn
      # and stay green; the 24h sweeper remains the backstop.
      - name: Reclaim orphaned draft twins (gh-1899)
        if: success()
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: bash scripts/release_draft_dedupe.sh "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" || echo "::warning::gh-1899 twin-draft dedupe failed — the 24h sweeper remains the backstop"

  # gh-1832 AC3: post-publish smoke. Probes (1) EVERY releases/(latest/)?
  # download/ URL the fa1.dev landing page exposes (site/index.html) and
  # (2) the full required set from scripts/release_required_assets.txt via
  # a 1-byte ranged GET each — red on anything but HTTP 200/206. Rides the
  # tag train only (PR runs never probe release URLs); a 404 here is the
  # owner-facing v1.0.635 symptom caught the same hour it appears.
  release-asset-smoke:
    name: Release asset smoke (landing links + required set)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: release-provenance
    timeout-minutes: 10
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.release-provenance.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release')
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Probe every landing-page release link
        run: bash scripts/assert_release_assets.sh --landing site/index.html
      - name: Probe the full required asset set
        env:
          GITHUB_REPOSITORY: ${{ github.repository }}
        run: bash scripts/assert_release_assets.sh --smoke "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"

  # Advance the vpinned release marker to the freshly signed tag. PURE
  # RELEASE-ARTIFACT MANIPULATION — no commits, no pushes: pin_release.sh
  # re-verifies the target's signature itself (fail-closed), then uploads
  # the PINNED_VERSION asset to the standing `vpinned` release. Runs after
  # release-provenance so the signed SHA256SUMS it checks are already
  # published. The marker is only a pointer — installers verify the pointed
  # release's signature against the committed trust anchor, so a tampered
  # marker degrades to a DoS, never a bad binary.
  install-pin-bump:
    name: Advance vpinned marker
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: release-provenance
    timeout-minutes: 10
    # always(): when release-provenance FAILS (e.g. the binaries/signature
    # upload race), plain needs-gating leaves this job SKIPPED — and a
    # `rerun --failed` never resurrects skipped jobs, so the marker stays
    # stale forever (v1.0.483: publish+provenance flaked, the recovery rerun
    # went green, the marker never advanced). With always() the job RUNS
    # even after a failed provenance: pin_release.sh's own pre-move
    # provenance gate (check_install_pin.sh with FA_PIN_TARGET) fails the
    # job loudly instead of moving the marker — and a FAILED job IS part of
    # rerun --failed, so the recovery cascade reaches it.
    if: >-
      always() && github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Point the vpinned marker at ${{ github.ref_name }}
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: bash scripts/pin_release.sh "${{ github.ref_name }}"

  installer-smoke:
    name: Installer smoke
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    needs: [binaries, release-provenance]
    timeout-minutes: 15
    # Depends on binaries — no !cancelled() needed here: the skip chain is
    # already broken upstream by the binaries job's own guard (fa#456).
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release'
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - os: windows-latest
            kind: ps1
          - os: ubuntu-latest
            kind: sh
          - os: macos-latest
            kind: sh
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Run the one-line installer (PowerShell)
        if: matrix.kind == 'ps1'
        shell: pwsh
        run: ./site/install.ps1

      - name: Run the one-line installer (sh)
        if: matrix.kind == 'sh'
        shell: bash
        env:
          FA_INSTALL_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}/fa-bin
        run: sh ./site/install.sh

# Daily auto-publish (issue #161): thin orchestrator over the existing
# publish channels. Each channel is an isolated leg — one leg failing never
# kills the others — and every failure self-files a deduplicated GitHub
# issue (label `bug`, assigned to the owner) that auto-closes when the leg
# goes green again. No publish logic is duplicated here: legs dispatch the
# existing workflows via `gh workflow run` and watch them.
#
#   testflight  build-mobile.yml   ios_content=all (the iOS half of the
#                                 mobile build)
#   play        build-mobile.yml   android_content=all,
#                                 android_track=beta (Android external
#                                 beta / open testing — issue #289 lifts
#                                 the standing "Android excluded" owner
#                                 decision for the release track; #947
#                                 adds the listing deploy — texts +
#                                 whole-set image replace + verify — so
#                                 the listing never trails the goldens;
#                                 the leg green-skips while the Play
#                                 secrets are absent)
#   pubdev      in-job OIDC publish, only when pubspec > pub.dev; otherwise
#               a green up-to-date check. The tag-time OIDC publish job
#               (ci.yml) stays the primary path; this leg is the catch-up +
#               loud-failure detector (e.g. expired publish credentials)
#   cli         build-macos.yml    desktop DMG + macOS CLI bundles +
#                                 extension, attached to the next-tag
#                                 release (version passed explicitly so
#                                 mobile/desktop never mint diverging tags)
#   windows     build-windows.yml windows-x64 app zip (fa-app-windows-x64.zip,
#                                 stable name), attached to the next-tag
#                                 release — the Windows counterpart of the
#                                 TestFlight leg: one release-quality GUI
#                                 app build per day (gh-2140)
#   website     pages.yml          fa1.dev (landing + web demo +
#                                 the /outlook add-in slice; gh-1684:
#                                 the extension zip moved to GitHub
#                                 Releases and is no longer site-hosted)
#   addin       office-addin.yml   manifest/taskpane acceptance suite; the
#                                 fa1.dev publish itself rides the website
#                                 leg (pages.yml assembles /outlook)
#
# Legs run only when main moved since the last GREEN daily run — skip-no-
# change is green-neutral, never red (#159 lesson). One exception (gh-1192):
# while main's pubspec version is not yet served by pub.dev the plan gate
# (scripts/daily_plan.sh) forces the legs anyway — a release-in-flight
# green must not become a skip baseline that stalls re-verification and
# rerun-recovery on a quiet main. Versioning stays the
# existing scheme: auto_release.sh patch-bumps + tags every main push
# (2h coalesce); the daily attaches mobile/desktop artifacts to the next
# tag and verifies/republishes pub.dev. See docs/ci.md.
#
# Pause: gh workflow disable daily-publish.yml -R IstiN/flutter_agent_harness

name: Daily auto-publish

run-name: "Daily auto-publish (${{ inputs.legs || 'all' }})"

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '17 5 * * *' # once daily, 05:17 UTC
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      legs:
        description: 'Leg(s) to run'
        type: choice
        default: all
        options:
          - all
          - testflight
          - play
          - pubdev
          - cli
          - windows
          - website
          - addin
      force:
        description: 'Run even if main has not moved since the last green daily'
        type: boolean
        default: false
      inject_failure:
        description: 'TEST ONLY — fail this leg before any dispatch, to exercise the self-filing issue cycle'

102:  plan:

422:  windows:
468:  website:
518:  addin:

662:  sweep-drafts:
681:  report:

version="${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}"
          # gh-2120 follow-up: the entry is BUILT as `fa` (bin/fa.dart), not
          # renamed — on Dart >=3.14 (native linux) the bundle is split
          # (thin launcher + libdartaot<exe>.so) and a post-build mv
          # desyncs the pair (`dartaotruntime: not an AOT snapshot`).
          dart build cli --target=bin/fa.dart --output=build/out
          chmod +x build/out/bundle/bin/fa
          echo "$version" > build/out/bundle/version.txt

      - name: Ad-hoc sign CLI binary
        run: |
          codesign --force --sign - build/out/bundle/bin/fa

      # gh-2040: the native fa-clip pasteboard helper rides the macOS CLI
      # bundle (bundle/bin/fa-clip, per-arch — this matrix builds each arch
      # on a native runner, AC8) so install.sh / fa update ship it beside
      # the binary and image paste never rides Apple Events.
      - name: Build fa-clip pasteboard helper (gh-2040)
        run: |
          bash scripts/build_fa_clip.sh build/out/bundle/bin/fa-clip
          codesign --force --sign - build/out/bundle/bin/fa-clip
          test -x build/out/bundle/bin/fa-clip

      - name: Archive and upload CLI bundle
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}
          # Matrix legs share GITHUB_JOB=build-macos-cli — the leg-suffixed
          # draft owner identity keeps the guard below scoped to the leg
          # that created the draft, never the sibling's mid-upload one.
          RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY: run/${{ github.run_id }}/job/${{ github.job }}-${{ matrix.arch }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          asset="fa-macos-${{ matrix.arch }}.tar.gz"
          tar -czf "$asset" -C build/out bundle
          ls -lh "$asset"

          # gh-1801 (rework): DRAFT-first, publish is PROVENANCE-OWNED.
          # The CLI tarball is a `fa update` asset, but servability needs
          # the SIGNED SHA256SUMS — which only the tag-run's
          # release-provenance job uploads (ci.yml). So: create the draft
          # lazily (curated notes via release_notes.sh + THIS leg's
          # draft-owner marker the guard below can reclaim), upload, and
          # let provenance own the --draft=false --latest flip.
          bash scripts/release_lazy_draft.sh "$RELEASE_TAG"
          # gh-2042 AC1: the immutability gate owns the attach — a
          # PUBLISHED release (the same-tag convergence race) skips
          # attached assets and refuses unattached fa-* assets loud
          # instead of silently drifting the signed SHA256SUMS.
          bash scripts/release_asset_gate.sh "$RELEASE_TAG" "$asset"

      # Draft lifecycle invariant (issue #282): this job creates releases,
      # so a failed/cancelled run must not leave one behind as a draft.
      # Leg-scoped (gh-1801): matches only THIS arch leg's marker.
      - name: Draft lifecycle guard (delete orphaned draft on failure)
        if: always() && job.status != 'success'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}
          RELEASE_DRAFT_IDENTITY: run/${{ github.run_id }}/job/${{ github.job }}-${{ matrix.arch }}
        run: bash scripts/release_draft_guard.sh "$RELEASE_TAG"

  build-extension:
    name: Build Chrome extension
    needs: version
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily cli watcher's budget arithmetic (#351).
    timeout-minutes: 30
    if: inputs.create_release == 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: write
      # gh-2026: defense-in-depth for the release_tag_mint.sh
      # train-verification probe (`gh run list` on the tag ref); the
      # probe itself authenticates with RELEASE_PAT (gh prefers
      # GH_TOKEN, which every mint-reachable call site exports), so
      # this grant matters only if the probe is ever switched to the
      # job token. Granted on every mint-reachable job.
      actions: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # Blobless full history: the lazy draft create (gh-1801 rework)
          # builds the release body via scripts/release_notes.sh — same
          # reason as release-macos's checkout (gh-1477).
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          # gh-1684 decision 4 (gate symmetry): the SAME exact patch pin
          # the pages.yml leg carried and the PR gate carries (#1431 —
          # the rev normalization absorbs canvaskit rev-hash churn, the
          # pin keeps every fa-extension.zip build comparable across
          # legs). The old unpinned `channel: stable` floated the engine
          # per run — one of the two ways the release and Pages legs
          # diverged.
          flutter-version: '3.50.0'
          channel: stable

      - name: dart pub get (root)
        run: dart pub get

      # browser_ext/dart is a separate package (path dep on this root), so
      # its pub get must follow the root's — same as browser-ext.yml.
      - name: dart pub get (browser_ext/dart)
        run: cd browser_ext/dart && dart pub get

      # Full artifact: SW agent (dart2js) + the Flutter panel app embedded,
      # exactly what "Load unpacked" expects. --clobber keeps the stable
      # asset name fa-extension.zip pointing at the newest build (the
      # landing page links it directly).
      - name: Build extension zip
        run: bash scripts/build_browser_ext.sh --with-app

      # AC1 (#1096): per-entry uncompressed size table + +5% budget gate
      # against the committed baseline (gh-2004: reseeded to the post-gemma
      # vendored-engines shape — transformers/webllm are intentional CWS
      # policy; growth beyond the floor fails the release).
      # Identical invocation as the PR-time gate (ci.yml
      # extension-size-gate): one baseline, one enforcement rule.
      - name: Size manifest + budget gate (fa-extension.zip)
        run: python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check build/fa-extension.zip --baseline scripts/size_budget/fa-extension.tsv

      - name: Upload extension to the release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          asset="fa-extension.zip"
          cp build/fa-extension.zip "$asset"

binaries:
    name: Build native binaries
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    needs: [release-dedupe, quality-gate]
    timeout-minutes: 45
    # Tag pushes (annotated, via PAT) and `release: published` events both
    # build the matrix. Since v0.1.370 the daily-publish plan creates
    # releases through the API — a lightweight tag with NO push event —
    # which silently starved linux/windows CLI assets (they existed only
    # while tags were still PAT-pushed, up to v0.1.369). The release event
    # fires for every creation path, so the matrix can never be starved
    # again.
    # gh-1625: on a deduped release twin the tag's own GREEN push run IS
    # the gate (the dedupe lookup fires only on conclusion == "success") —
    # the twin's quality legs all skip, so the explicit
    # `result == 'success'` check is ORed with the dedupe arm. The push
    # twin and the dedupe=false old-tag release still gate the matrix on
    # the full quality gate exactly as before.
    # Same !cancelled() pattern as the release job: the transitive skip
    # through always()-quality-gate starved this matrix on tag pushes and
    # release events alike (fa#456) — no linux/windows CLI assets since
    # v0.1.370. The explicit gate check keeps failed-gate runs from
    # building publishable binaries.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() &&
      (needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' ||
      (github.event_name == 'release' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe == 'true')) &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release')
    permissions:
      contents: write # attach assets to the GitHub Release
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - runner: windows-latest
            os: windows
            arch: x64
            archive: zip
          - runner: macos-latest
            os: macos
            arch: arm64
            archive: tar
          # Intel Mac runner (macos-13 is retired; AOT cannot cross-compile
          # macos_x64 from arm64 — only linux_* targets cross).
          - runner: macos-15-intel
            os: macos
            arch: x64
            archive: tar
          - runner: ubuntu-latest
            os: linux
            arch: x64
            archive: tar
          # Native ARM64 runner — dart build cli does not cross-compile.
          - runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm
            os: linux
            arch: arm64
=== sweep-drafts job ===
  sweep-drafts:
    name: Sweep stale release drafts
    needs: plan
    if: always() # even when plan failed or all legs skipped
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: write # delete draft releases
      actions: read # name each swept draft's creating run (gh run list 403s without it, review of #294)
      issues: write # deduplicated self-closing sweep issue
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Delete drafts older than 24h and file the dedup issue
        run: bash scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh

  # ── Report + self-healing issues ─────────────────────────────────────────
  report:
    name: Summary + self-filed issues
    needs: [plan, testflight, play, pubdev, cli, website, addin]
    if: always() # runs even when plan failed, so plan failures enter the self-healing loop too
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read
      issues: write
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Job summary table and issue lifecycle
        env:
          NEXT_TAG: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.next_tag }}
          PLAN_RESULT: ${{ needs.plan.result }}
          DAILY_PUBLISH_ASSIGNEE: ai-teammate

arguments.content:
# Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: A pipeline-staged release draft (`v1.0.728`) whose publish owner is the tag train survived a FAILED tag train for >24h and was swept by the daily draft sweeper (gh-2230) — the release never shipped and the sweep issue fires every time this shape recurs.

**Root cause**: The issue #282 draft lifecycle invariant is enforced only **per creating job**: every job that creates a release draft carries `scripts/release_draft_guard.sh` under `if: always() && job.status != 'success'` (ci.yml `binaries`, build-macos.yml, build-mobile.yml). But since the gh-1801 draft-staging rework the draft's **publish owner is a different run**: the ci.yml tag train's `release-provenance` job (the sole publish point — `--draft=false --latest` flip). When the tag train fails **upstream of the publish point**, no job that owns a guard has failed:

1. Daily `cli` leg → build-macos.yml mints tag `v1.0.728` and its `build-macos-cli` legs stage the draft (`scripts/release_lazy_draft.sh`, marker `release-draft-owner: run/43680583152/job/...`) — creating run 43680583152 **succeeds**, so its guard never fires.
2. The tag train (ci.yml on the tag ref, run 43680913877) fails at Core tests shard 3/4 → `quality-gate` red → `binaries` skipped (`needs.quality-gate.result == 'success'` gate) → `release-provenance` **skipped** (needs binaries success) → the `--draft=false --latest` publish flip never runs. (`install-pin-bump` failing "Advance vpinned marker" is the designed loud provenance-gate failure, not the root cause.)
3. Nothing reclaims the draft: the failed train is superseded and never rerun, `verify_pubdev_release.sh` heals the LATEST tag only. The per-job guards are all in jobs that succeeded; there is **no train-level guard** keyed on the publish point not running. The draft rots exactly 24h until `scripts/sweep_stale_drafts.sh` deletes it and files the recurring sweep issue.

**Impact**: Every failed tag train with a pre-staged draft orphans the staged release for ≥24h (draft assets unpublished, tag unpublished); the sweeper files a recurring `[daily-publish] stale release drafts swept` issue (gh-2230) and the release silently never ships. Conditions: any red in the train's quality legs while a draft for the trained tag exists.

**Fix approach**: Add the missing **train-level** draft lifecycle guard:

- New `scripts/release_train_draft_guard.sh <tag>`: deletes drafts for the trained tag whose well-formed `release-draft-owner:` marker run is **completed** (a superseded failed train is never rerun, so nobody else will ever publish them; draft assets are unpublished by definition — #282 E2; the git tag is never touched). Fail-safe keeps: drafts owned by still-in-flight runs (a concurrent creator leg may be mid-upload), unmarked/human drafts (E1 — the sweeper stays the backstop), and any owner-run status lookup failure (never delete blind).
- New ci.yml job `train-draft-guard`: `needs: release-provenance` (runs only after the publish point settled — success, failure, or skip) + `if: always()` on tag-push/release events; grants `contents: write` (delete) + `actions: read` (owner-run status probe), same permission model as the sweeper's `sweep-drafts` job.
- Pinned in `test/release_hygiene_test.dart` (behavioral stub-gh tests + static workflow lint), and documented in `docs/ci.md` § Release hygiene.

**Previous attempt**: None — first fix for this recurrence shape (gh-2105 taught the sweeper to *diagnose* failed trains; this fix makes the train *clean up* after itself).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Train-level draft lifecycle guard (issue #282, gh-2230): the ci.yml tag
# train is the PUBLISH OWNER of every staged draft (gh-1801 rework — the
# release-provenance job is the sole `--draft=false --latest` flip point),
# but the per-creating-job guards (scripts/release_draft_guard.sh) cover
# only their own job's failure. A train that dies UPSTREAM of the publish
# point (core tests -> quality-gate red -> binaries skipped ->
# release-provenance skipped) left the staged draft orphaned: the creating
# run's jobs all succeeded (their guards never fire), the failed train is
# superseded and never rerun, and verify_pubdev_release.sh heals the LATEST
# tag only — so the draft rotted exactly 24h until the daily sweeper
# deleted it and filed the recurring sweep issue (gh-2230, v1.0.728).
#
# Called from the ci.yml `train-draft-guard` job, which needs
# release-provenance and runs with `if: always()`: by the time this script
# runs, the publish point has settled (success, failure, or skip) and every
# in-train draft-creating job (binaries, web-spa, build-extension) has
# settled with it.
#
# Deletes (by release id, the tag itself is never touched — drafts may
# carry an empty tag_name, and the id-based API delete is what the sweeper
# uses) only drafts for THIS train's tag whose well-formed
# `release-draft-owner: run/<id>/job/<name>` marker names a COMPLETED run:
# a superseded failed train will never publish them, and draft assets are
# unpublished by definition (issue #282 E2 — published releases are the
# artifact store). Fail-safe keeps — the sweeper remains the backstop:
#   - drafts owned by a run that is still queued/in_progress (a concurrent
#     creator leg, e.g. build-macos.yml from the daily cli leg, may be
#     mid-upload — the train can fail faster than a sibling workflow
#     finishes attaching);
#   - unmarked drafts (no marker = no proof of pipeline ownership — E1,
#     gh-2008; a human draft is never deleted here);
#   - any owner-run status lookup failure (never delete blind).
#
# Env: GITHUB_REPOSITORY; needs `contents: write` (release delete) and
# `actions: read` (owner-run status probe — same grant model as the
# sweep-drafts job, review of #294).
set -euo pipefail

tag="${1:?usage: release_train_draft_guard.sh <tag>}"
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"

# ── inventory: drafts for THIS train's tag ──────────────────────────────────
# gh api --paginate emits one JSON array per page; the jq stream filter
# flattens them (same shape as sweep_stale_drafts.sh). Ownership-marker
# parsing: a bare capture(...)? on a non-matching body yields an EMPTY
# stream, so the array wrapper keeps exactly one (possibly empty) value
# per draft row.
rows=$(gh api --paginate "repos/$repo/releases" | jq -r --arg tag "$tag" '
  [ .[] | select(.draft == true and (.tag_name // "") == $tag)
    | { id: (.id | tostring),
        run: ([ (.body // "")
                | capture("release-draft-owner: run/(?<run>[0-9]+)/")?
                | .run ]
              | .[0] // "") } ]
  | .[]
  | [ .id, .run ] | @tsv')

deleted=0
kept=0
while IFS=$'\t' read -r id marker_run; do
  [ -n "$id" ] || continue
  if [ -z "$marker_run" ]; then
    echo "::warning::train draft guard: draft $id for $tag carries no release-draft-owner marker — no proof of pipeline ownership (possibly a human draft, E1); leaving it to the 24h sweeper (issue #282)"
    kept=$((kept + 1))
    continue
  fi
  # Fail-safe lifecycle check: delete only when the owner run has
  # COMPLETED. A non-completed status — or any lookup failure (403 without
  # actions:read, API blip) — keeps the draft: never delete blind.
  status=$(gh run view "$marker_run" --repo "$repo" --json status --jq .status 2>/dev/null || echo "")
  if [ "$status" != "completed" ]; then
    echo "::warning::train draft guard: draft $id for $tag is owned by run $marker_run (status: ${status:-<lookup failed>}) — the owner is not provably done; refusing to delete a possibly mid-upload draft. The 24h sweeper remains the backstop (issue #282)"
    kept=$((kept + 1))
    continue
  fi
  gh api -X DELETE "repos/$repo/releases/$id"
  echo "::warning::train draft guard: deleted draft $id for $tag (owner run $marker_run completed; this failed train is superseded and will never publish it — a rerun cannot resurrect skipped jobs). Draft assets are unpublished by definition; the git tag is untouched (issue #282, gh-2230)"
  deleted=$((deleted + 1))
done <<< "$rows"

echo "train draft guard: deleted=$deleted kept=$kept for $tag"

The stub: `run` case → first if: `[ "$2" = "list" ]` — no; elif `--json jobs` — no; my new elif `--json status` — should match `printf '%s' "$*" | grep -q -- '--json status'`... Wait — `$*` includes `--jq .status` and `--json status` — matches. It should cat run-status.json — NOT planted in this test → default `{"status":"completed"}` → `jq .status`... wait — the script pipes: `gh run view ... --json status --jq .status`. The stub outputs the JSON `{"status":"completed"}` — but the `--jq .status` is passed TO GH, not executed locally! The stub just cats the raw JSON; the script captures `status=$(gh run view ... --jq .status ...)` — with real gh, `--jq` filters server-side output... actually gh's --jq filters the JSON client-side. With the STUB, gh doesn't apply --jq; the output is the RAW JSON `{"status":"completed"}` — so `$status` = `{"status":"completed"}` ≠ "completed" → keep!

How do the existing scripts handle this? The sweper: `gh run view "$train_id" --repo "$repo" --json jobs | jq -r '...'` — it pipes to an EXPLICIT jq, because the stub doesn't implement --jq. So the stub serves PRE-FILTERED scalar content for --jq cases (release-state.txt = "true").

Option (a) matches the sweper's established pattern AND works against real gh (gh outputs JSON, jq filters). With the stub, `gh run view ... --json status` (no --jq arg) → stub still cats run-status.json (grep matches --json status). Then `| jq -r .status` filters → "completed".

```bash
status=$(gh run view "$marker_run" --repo "$repo" --json status 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.status // empty' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
``

runs the mobile and macOS legs concurrently on the same derived tag, and
  a failed leg's guard must never destroy the sibling leg's mid-upload
  draft (foreign or unmarked drafts are left to the sweeper). Pinned by

- **Train-level draft lifecycle guard** (gh-2230) — the per-job guards
  above fire only on their own job's failure, but since the gh-1801
  rework the staged draft's publish owner is the TAG TRAIN (ci.yml's
  `release-provenance`, the sole publish point). A train that dies
  upstream of the publish point (core tests → quality-gate red → binaries
  skipped → provenance skipped) used to orphan the staged draft until the
  24h sweeper reclaimed it and filed the recurring sweep issue. ci.yml now
  carries a `train-draft-guard` job (`needs: release-provenance`,
  `if: always()` on tag-push/release events) running
  `scripts/release_train_draft_guard.sh`: it deletes drafts for the
  trained tag whose well-formed ownership marker names a COMPLETED run (a
  superseded failed train is never rerun, so nobody else would ever
  publish them; the git tag is untouched). Fail-safe keeps — in-flight
  owner runs (a concurrent creator leg may be mid-upload), unmarked/human
  drafts (E1), and any owner-status lookup failure (never delete blind);
  the sweeper remains the backstop. Grants `contents: write` +
  `actions: read`, same stub-enforced model as the sweep-drafts job.

content.text:
# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- fix(gh-2194): the fa1.dev landing page no longer exposes two broken
  Windows download links. The windows-release landing (#2158) deep-linked
  `releases/latest/download/fa-app-windows-x64.zip` / `.msix`, but those
  assets belong to the daily `build-windows` leg — deliberately outside
  `scripts/release_required_assets.txt` — and the leg has not attached
  them yet, so every train-cut `latest` 404'd both links; the v1.0.729
  release run's gh-1832 asset smoke caught it and red'd the tag. The
  Windows button now follows the macOS button's pattern (release page,
  which always lists the windows app zip/msix/cer once shipped plus the
  guaranteed `fa-windows-x64.zip` CLI archive), the msix deep link is
  gone, and a new offline guard
  (`test/site/landing_deep_links_test.dart`) pins the contract: every
  `latest/download` deep link on the landing page must name a
  required-set asset — PRs can no longer land links only the tag train
  can falsify (`#2194`)
- feat(gh-2103): compaction digest provenance — summaries can no longer
  launder tool-controlled text into trusted memory. The audit verdict: the
  typed pipeline is sound (the judge sees typed ledger lines, the fold input
  keeps `[User]:`/`[Tool result]:` labels, request candidates come only from
  real non-synthetic user turns), but digest TEXT could copy tool-controlled
  instructions into `## Open User Requests` unmarked. Three layers: every
  digest/checkpoint prompt now carries the origin-provenance duty (asks only
  from real `[User]:` turns; instruction-shaped tool output, forged
  `[User]:` labels and "USER INSTRUCTION" framing are never user intent;
  verbatim tool quotes carry a `[from toolResult]` mark); `sanitizeSummary`
shellcheck clean

**Refinement (recovery-vessel case):** `release-provenance` FAILED (vs. skipped) is rerunnable via `gh run rerun --failed` — the existing gh-1899 comment explicitly keeps the draft as the "rerun --failed recovery vessel" on a red provenance. Only a **skipped** publish point (needs failed/skipped — never resurrectable by rerun) makes deletion correct. I'll gate the delete on the publish point's settled result, passed explicitly into the script.

arguments.newText:
tag="${1:?usage: release_train_draft_guard.sh <tag>}"
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"

# The publish point's settled result (exported by the workflow from
# needs.release-provenance.result). Deletion is only correct when the
# publish point is UNREACHABLE: `skipped` means its needs (binaries) failed
# or were skipped, and `gh run rerun --failed` never resurrects skipped
# jobs — nobody will ever publish this draft. A FAILED or CANCELLED
# provenance IS rerunnable, and the staged draft is then the rerun
# --failed recovery vessel (the gh-1899 convention in ci.yml's success-path
# dedupe step: "a red provenance keeps the draft as the rerun --failed
# recovery vessel") — keep it; the 24h sweeper reclaims it if the train is
# never recovered. Unset (wiring broken) keeps too: fail-safe, never
# delete blind — the sweeper backstops the kept drafts either way.
result="${PROVENANCE_RESULT:-}"
if [ "$result" != "skipped" ]; then
  echo "::warning::train draft guard: release-provenance ${result:-<result not exported>} — a rerunnable (non-skipped) publish failure keeps the staged draft as the rerun --failed recovery vessel (gh-1899 convention); the 24h sweeper reclaims it if the train is never recovered (issue #282)"
  exit 0
fi

# settled — needs release-provenance + always(), so it fires on failed AND
  # cancelled trains and never on the success path's result (the script
  # no-ops on a published release). The script deletes ONLY when the
  # publish point is unreachable (result == 'skipped' — rerun --failed
  # never resurrects skipped jobs): drafts for THIS train's tag whose
  # owner-marker run has completed (scripts/release_train_draft_guard.sh).
  # A failed/cancelled provenance is rerunnable, so the staged draft stays
  # as the rerun --failed recovery vessel (gh-1899 convention). In-flight
  # owner runs and unmarked/human drafts stay with the sweeper (E1).
  train-draft-guard:
    name: Train draft lifecycle guard
    needs: release-provenance
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    if: >-
      always() &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release')
    permissions:
      contents: write # delete the orphaned staged draft (issue #282 E2)
      actions: read # probe the draft-owner marker run's status (gh-2008 pattern)
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Delete drafts the failed train will never publish
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          PROVENANCE_RESULT: ${{ needs.release-provenance.result }}
        run: bash scripts/release_train_draft_guard.sh "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"

arguments.newText:
**Fix approach**: Add the missing **train-level** draft lifecycle guard:

- New `scripts/release_train_draft_guard.sh <tag>`: runs at the end of the ci.yml tag train with the publish point's settled result exported (`PROVENANCE_RESULT=${{ needs.release-provenance.result }}`). Deletes drafts for the trained tag ONLY when that result is `skipped` — the publish point is unreachable (its needs failed/were skipped and `gh run rerun --failed` never resurrects skipped jobs), so nobody will ever publish them. Delete criteria per draft: well-formed `release-draft-owner:` marker naming a **completed** run (draft assets are unpublished by definition — #282 E2; the git tag is never touched). Fail-safe keeps: a FAILED/CANCELLED provenance (rerunnable — the draft stays as the `rerun --failed` recovery vessel, per the gh-1899 convention already in ci.yml), drafts owned by still-in-flight runs (a concurrent creator leg may be mid-upload), unmarked/human drafts (E1 — the sweeper stays the backstop), any owner-run status lookup failure, and an unexported result (never delete blind).
- New ci.yml job `train-draft-guard`: `needs: release-provenance` (runs only after the publish point settled — success, failure, or skip) + `if: always()` on tag-push/release events; grants `contents: write` (delete) + `actions: read` (owner-run status probe), same permission model as the sweeper's `sweep-drafts` job.

### Root Cause

The issue #282 draft lifecycle invariant was enforced only per **creating job** (`release_draft_guard.sh` in the same job as the draft create), but since the gh-1801 rework the staged draft's publish owner is a different run — the ci.yml tag train's `release-provenance` job (the sole `--draft=false --latest` flip). For `v1.0.728`: the creating run (daily `cli` leg → build-macos.yml, run 43680583152) **succeeded**, while the tag train (run 43680913877) failed upstream of the publish point (Core tests shard 3/4 → quality-gate red → `binaries` skipped → `release-provenance` skipped) — no guarded job ever failed, the publish flip never ran, and the draft rotted until the 24h sweeper deleted it and filed the recurring sweep issue.

### Fix

- `scripts/release_train_draft_guard.sh` (new): deletes drafts for the trained tag whose well-formed `release-draft-owner:` marker names a **completed** run — only when the publish point's settled result is `skipped` (unreachable: `rerun --failed` never resurrects skipped jobs). Fail-safe keeps: failed/cancelled provenance (rerunnable → the draft stays as the `rerun --failed` recovery vessel, gh-1899 convention), in-flight owner runs, unmarked/human drafts (E1), lookup failures, unset result. The git tag is never touched.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (new `train-draft-guard` job): `needs: release-provenance` + `always()` on tag-push/release events; exports `PROVENANCE_RESULT=${{ needs.release-provenance.result }}`; grants `contents: write` + `actions: read` (same model as `sweep-drafts`).
- `docs/ci.md` § Release hygiene + `CHANGELOG.md` `## Unreleased` entries; pinned in `test/release_hygiene_test.dart`.

### Test Coverage

- `test/release_hygiene_test.dart` gh-2230 group — 11 new tests (delete/keep decision matrix + static workflow lint) — PASSED (written first, confirmed failing before the fix)
- `dart test test/release_hygiene_test.dart`: 68 passed, 0 failed
- Full deterministic suite (`dart test`): see CI run on this PR
- Script also smoke-verified directly: tag-scoped delete, in-flight keep, published no-op

### Notes

- The ticket's operational half — "rerun the train if the tag should still ship" — stays a release-owner decision: `v1.0.728`'s Core tests shard 3/4 + Quality gate failures need investigation, and with `binaries`/`release-provenance` skipped, a `rerun --failed` cannot resurrect them; the next auto-release tag supersedes it. The sweep issue auto-closes on the next clean sweep.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Train-level draft lifecycle guard (issue #282, gh-2230): the ci.yml tag
# train is the PUBLISH OWNER of every staged draft (gh-1801 rework — the
# release-provenance job is the sole `--draft=false --latest` flip point),
# but the per-creating-job guards (scripts/release_draft_guard.sh) cover
# only their own job's failure. A train that dies UPSTREAM of the publish
# point (core tests -> quality-gate red -> binaries skipped ->
# release-provenance skipped) left the staged draft orphaned: the creating
# run's jobs all succeeded (their guards never fire), the failed train is
# superseded and never rerun, and verify_pubdev_release.sh heals the LATEST
# tag only — so the draft rotted exactly 24h until the daily sweeper
# deleted it and filed the recurring sweep issue (gh-2230, v1.0.728).
#
# Called from the ci.yml `train-draft-guard` job, which needs
# release-provenance and runs with `if: always()`: by the time this script
# runs, the publish point has settled (success, failure, or skip) and every
# in-train draft-creating job (binaries, web-spa, build-extension) has
# settled with it.
#
# Deletes (by release id, the tag itself is never touched — drafts may
# carry an empty tag_name, and the id-based API delete is what the sweeper
# uses) only drafts for THIS train's tag whose well-formed
# `release-draft-owner: run/<id>/job/<name>` marker names a COMPLETED run:
# a superseded failed train will never publish them, and draft assets are
# unpublished by definition (issue #282 E2 — published releases are the
# artifact store). Fail-safe keeps — the sweeper remains the backstop:
#   - drafts owned by a run that is still queued/in_progress (a concurrent
#     creator leg, e.g. build-macos.yml from the daily cli leg, may be
#     mid-upload — the train can fail faster than a sibling workflow
#     finishes attaching);
#   - unmarked drafts (no marker = no proof of pipeline ownership — E1,
#     gh-2008; a human draft is never deleted here);
#   - any owner-run status lookup failure (never delete blind).
#
# Env: GITHUB_REPOSITORY; needs `contents: write` (release delete) and
# `actions: read` (owner-run status probe — same grant model as the
# sweep-drafts job, review of #294).
set -euo pipefail

tag="${1:?usage: release_train_draft_guard.sh <tag>}"
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:?GITHUB_REPOSITORY must be set}"

# The publish point's settled result (exported by the workflow from
# needs.release-provenance.result). Deletion is only correct when the
# publish point is UNREACHABLE: `skipped` means its needs (binaries) failed
# or were skipped, and `gh run rerun --failed` never resurrects skipped
# jobs — nobody will ever publish this draft. A FAILED or CANCELLED
# provenance IS rerunnable, and the staged draft is then the rerun
# --failed recovery vessel (the gh-1899 convention in ci.yml's success-path
# dedupe step: "a red provenance keeps the draft as the rerun --failed
# recovery vessel") — keep it; the 24h sweeper reclaims it if the train is
# never recovered. Unset (wiring broken) keeps too: fail-safe, never
# delete blind — the sweeper backstops the kept drafts either way.
result="${PROVENANCE_RESULT:-}"
if [ "$result" != "skipped" ]; then
  echo "::warning::train draft guard: release-provenance ${result:-<result not exported>} — a rerunnable (non-skipped) publish failure keeps the staged draft as the rerun --failed recovery vessel (gh-1899 convention); the 24h sweeper reclaims it if the train is never recovered (issue #282)"
  exit 0
fi

# ── inventory: drafts for THIS train's tag ──────────────────────────────────
# gh api --paginate emits one JSON array per page; the jq stream filter
# flattens them (same shape as sweep_stale_drafts.sh). Ownership-marker
# parsing: a bare capture(...)? on a non-matching body yields an EMPTY
# stream, so the array wrapper keeps exactly one (possibly empty) value
# per draft row.
rows=$(gh api --paginate "repos/$repo/releases" | jq -r --arg tag "$tag" '
  [ .[] | select(.draft == true and (.tag_name // "") == $tag)
    | { id: (.id | tostring),
        run: ([ (.body // "")
                | capture("release-draft-owner: run/(?<run>[0-9]+)/")?
                | .run ]
              | .[0] // "") } ]
  | .[]
  | [ .id, .run ] | @tsv')

deleted=0
kept=0
while IFS=$'\t' read -r id marker_run; do
  [ -n "$id" ] || continue
  if [ -z "$marker_run" ]; then
    echo "::warning::train draft guard: draft $id for $tag carries no release-draft-owner marker — no proof of pipeline ownership (possibly a human draft, E1); leaving it to the 24h sweeper (issue #282)"
    kept=$((kept + 1))
    continue
  fi
  # Fail-safe lifecycle check: delete only when the owner run has
  # COMPLETED. A non-completed status — or any lookup failure (403 without
  # actions:read, API blip) — keeps the draft: never delete blind.
  # Explicit jq pipe (not gh's --jq): mirrors sweep_stale_drafts.sh, where
  # every JSON probe is filtered by a real jq stage.
  status=$(gh run view "$marker_run" --repo "$repo" --json status 2>/dev/null \
    | jq -r '.status // empty' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
  if [ "$status" != "completed" ]; then
    echo "::warning::train draft guard: draft $id for $tag is owned by run $marker_run (status: ${status:-<lookup failed>}) — the owner is not provably done; refusing to delete a possibly mid-upload draft. The 24h sweeper remains the backstop (issue #282)"
    kept=$((kept + 1))
    continue
  fi
  gh api -X DELETE "repos/$repo/releases/$id"
  echo "::warning::train draft guard: deleted draft $id for $tag (owner run $marker_run completed; this failed train is superseded and will never publish it — a rerun cannot resurrect skipped jobs). Draft assets are unpublished by definition; the git tag is untouched (issue #282, gh-2230)"
  deleted=$((deleted + 1))
done <<< "$rows"

echo "train draft guard: deleted=$deleted kept=$kept for $tag"
